content: Postgres alone is sufficient for run mutual exclusion; no Redis/ZooKeeper. SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (PG 9.5+) turns a table into a queue and auto-releases the lock on worker crash via transaction rollback, but does not enforce global constraints (e.g. max-N concurrent) - use pg_advisory_xact_lock for those. Key caveat: never hold a transaction open across a multi-minute/hour worker call (idle-in-transaction bloat, connection exhaustion, no recovery until tx dies). Instead use a lease: columns locked_by/locked_at/lock_expires_at claimed by conditional UPDATE ... WHERE locked_by IS NULL OR lock_expires_at < now(), rowcount==1 means acquired; heartbeat the expiry during the call; a dead process's lease just expires. Back every state write with a guarded UPDATE ... WHERE status = :expected (rowcount 0 = someone else advanced).
